greeting: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen. Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ, who gathers us in His love today.
penitential:
Lord Jesus, you seek the lost and bring them home: Lord, have mercy.
Christ Jesus, you rejoice over every soul that finds its way to you: Christ, have mercy.
Lord Jesus, you are the Shepherd who carries us on your shoulders: Lord, have mercy.
psalm_response: Let hearts rejoice who search for the Lord.
homily:
We begin today by looking at a very small, very ordinary thing: a key. Think of the way a key feels in your hand—cold, jagged, weighted with the promise of access. We all have keys. We have keys to our homes, our cars, our offices. We spend a good portion of our lives looking for them, don’t we? We pat our pockets, we check the bowl by the door, we retrace our steps because we know that without the key, the door remains a barrier. It is a simple object, but it holds the power to change everything. It is the difference between standing outside in the cold and being safely inside, where the light is on and the people we love are waiting.

I want you to hold onto this image: the key. It is the image of the search—the relentless, hopeful, determined search for what is missing. It is an image of a God who refuses to let a single door remain locked between His heart and yours.

Let us speak the truth of the heart before we look for the comfort. Alan, Thao, Ryan, and all of you who carry the light of Benjamin Vo in your souls: it has been four months since Ben crossed the threshold of this world into the next. We know the reality of your quiet house. We know the moments when the silence becomes a weight, when the habits of a lifetime—the coding, the aviation spotting, the simple joy of a shared meal—are suddenly interrupted by the sharp, cold realization that he is not there in the way he once was. You are grieving. You are carrying a cross that feels far too heavy for human shoulders. You are allowed to be tired. You are allowed to be angry at the unfairness of a world that takes a boy of such brilliant promise. You are allowed to be human.

There is a temptation, when we carry this kind of sorrow, to look back at the path we walked and wonder if we missed a sign. We wonder if we could have seen something earlier, or done something differently, or if we failed in some hidden way. Let us lift that stone from your hearts right now. You missed nothing. You were the parents and the brother that Benjamin was given. You loved him with a completeness that filled his fifteen years with the richness of the world. You walked the globe with him, you shared the meals, you witnessed the brilliance of his mind and the gentleness of his spirit. God does not accuse you, and you must not accuse yourselves. Some sorrows in this fragile world arrive entirely beyond human reach, untouched by anything anyone did or failed to do. You are not to blame. Let that heavy stone fall to the ground; you are absolved. You were faithful. You were present. You were love in action.

Now, let the Gospel break in. Look at the shepherd. He has ninety-nine sheep, but he is fixated on the one. He does not count his losses and move on. He does not tell himself that the risk is too high or the effort is too great. He leaves the ninety-nine in the desert and goes after the lost one until he finds it. And when he finds it? He does not scold it. He does not drag it. He sets it on his shoulders. Think of that weight. The shepherd is carrying the sheep, bearing the burden of its weakness, feeling the warmth of its life against his own neck. He is bringing it home. Jesus is telling us that God’s love is not a passive thing. It is a search. It is a pursuit. It is the act of a heart that refuses to be whole until every single one of His own is safely gathered in.

Benjamin was a boy who understood the beauty of that kind of pursuit. Think of his brilliant, searching mind—the way he mastered mathematics, the way he dived into the complexities of cloud infrastructure, or how he coded his own games in his GitHub repository. He loved the logic of systems, the way a problem could be solved if you just worked at it long enough. But think of the gentleness of his spirit, which was the true architecture of his life. Think of the way he loved to look at airplanes, dreaming of his ‘con chim airlines.’ He wasn’t just looking at metal and engines; he was looking at the horizon, looking for the next place to explore, the next connection to be made. That is the boy you raised. That is the boy who is now at the banquet of heaven, interceding for you. He is not a memory; he is a living soul, fully alive in the love of God. He has found the destination he was searching for, and he is waiting for the rest of his family to arrive.

Ryan, you are a brother who carries a unique, holy weight. You know the memories better than anyone. You know the games you coded, the dreams you shared, the simple, everyday life of being brothers. You are not just a brother who remains; you are a brother who continues the story. When you look at the sky, when you think of the future, remember that you are not doing it alone. You are carrying the legacy of his joy. You are a witness to the world that love is not a finite resource. It is a well that never runs dry. Keep being the boy who reaches out. Keep being the one who values the small, human moments. You are a vital part of this family of four, and your life is a testament to the fact that love is the most durable thing we possess.

We hear in the letter to the Philippians today: ‘Whatever gains I had, these I have come to consider a loss because of Christ. More than that, I even consider everything as a loss because of the supreme good of knowing Christ Jesus my Lord.’ This is the turn of the heart. Paul is not saying that his heritage or his accomplishments were evil; he is saying that in the light of Christ, they are no longer the source of his security. He has found a greater key. He has found the only thing that opens the door to eternal life. When we lose someone as precious as Benjamin, we feel as though we have lost everything. And in a sense, we have lost the version of the world we knew. But in that emptiness, there is a new space created. There is a room in our hearts that is now reserved entirely for the hope of heaven. It is a room that only God can fill.

There is a peace that comes from knowing that we are held. It is not a peace that takes away the pain, but it is a peace that keeps us from being destroyed by it. It is the peace of knowing that Benjamin is waiting. He is waiting in the light, he is waiting in the place where there is no more struggling, no more darkness, only the clear, bright presence of the Father. He is waiting for you with that same sweet, gentle smile that you remember so vividly. That smile is the sign that the work is going well. That smile is the promise that the reunion is certain. He is a light in the world, and he is shining for you. He is the sheep that was found, and he is now resting on the shoulders of the Good Shepherd.

So, what do you carry out the door today? Not a summary, not a heavy burden, but one small, doable thing: when the grief rises and the house feels too quiet, pause. Close your eyes. Imagine the Lord reaching into the silence, and imagine Benjamin smiling at you from the other side. Let yourself be gathered. Trust that you are held. And walk out into the world with the quiet, unshakeable hope that the love you share is the most powerful force in the universe. It is stronger than death. It is more enduring than time. And it is the very thing that will bring you home to each other. You are not a broken family. You are a family of four, and you are being held in the palm of God's hand. Keep your heart open to that truth. Keep your eyes on the light. And remember that he is watching over you, always, with love that knows no end. Amen.
spiritual_communion: My Jesus, I believe that You are present in the Most Holy Sacrament. I love You above all things, and I desire to receive You into my soul. Since I cannot at this moment receive You sacramentally, come at least spiritually into my heart. I embrace You as if You were already there and unite myself wholly to You. Never permit me to be separated from You. Amen.
closing: May the Lord bless you and keep you, may He make His face shine upon you and be gracious to you, and may He give you His peace. Amen.
petition_call: For all our intentions, we pray to the Lord.
standing_petitions: For our beloved Benjamin Vo and all who have gone before us marked with the sign of faith, that they may rest forever in the light and peace of Christ, we pray to the Lord.
For all who are grieving and carrying the heavy cross of loss, that the Lord may console them with His presence and fill their hearts with the hope of the resurrection, we pray to the Lord.

readings.label: Reading 1
readings.text:
Brothers and sisters:
We are the circumcision, 
we who worship through the Spirit of God,
who boast in Christ Jesus and do not put our confidence in flesh,
although I myself have grounds for confidence even in the flesh.If anyone else thinks he can be confident in flesh, all the more can I.  
Circumcised on the eighth day,
of the race of Israel, of the tribe of Benjamin,
a Hebrew of Hebrew parentage,
in observance of the law a Pharisee,
in zeal I persecuted the Church,
in righteousness based on the law I was blameless.But whatever gains I had,
these I have come to consider a loss because of Christ.
More than that, I even consider everything as a loss
because of the supreme good of knowing Christ Jesus my Lord.

readings.label: Responsorial Psalm
readings.text:
R. (3b) Let hearts rejoice who search for the Lord.
or:
R. Alleluia.
Sing to him, sing his praise,
proclaim all his wondrous deeds.
Glory in his holy name;
rejoice, O hearts that seek the LORD!
R. Let hearts rejoice who search for the Lord.
or:
R. Alleluia.
Look to the LORD in his strength;
seek to serve him constantly.
Recall the wondrous deeds that he has wrought,
his portents, and the judgments he has uttered.
R. Let hearts rejoice who search for the Lord.
or:
R. Alleluia.
You descendants of Abraham, his servants,
sons of Jacob, his chosen ones!
He, the LORD, is our God;
throughout the earth his judgments prevail.
R. Let hearts rejoice who search for the Lord.
or:
R. Alleluia.

readings.label: Gospel
readings.text:
The tax collectors and sinners were all drawing near to listen to Jesus,
but the Pharisees and scribes began to complain, saying,
“This man welcomes sinners and eats with them.” 
So Jesus addressed this parable to them.
“What man among you having a hundred sheep and losing one of them
would not leave the ninety-nine in the desert
and go after the lost one until he finds it?
And when he does find it,
he sets it on his shoulders with great joy
and, upon his arrival home,
he calls together his friends and neighbors and says to them,
‘Rejoice with me because I have found my lost sheep.’ 
I tell you, in just the same way
there will be more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents
than over ninety-nine righteous people
who have no need of repentance.“Or what woman having ten coins and losing one
would not light a lamp and sweep the house,
searching carefully until she finds it?
And when she does find it,
she calls together her friends and neighbors
and says to them,
‘Rejoice with me because I have found the coin that I lost.’ 
In just the same way, I tell you,
there will be rejoicing among the angels of God
over one sinner who repents.”

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Hey Ben - Been dreaming about you a lot. Hope you're having fun up in heaven. Please look after our family. Remember to come say hi daily. We miss you so much!

Ben ơi, trong giấc ngủ anh Huy đã thấy Ben về thăm anh, trao cho anh lời cầu nguyện để hai anh em mình lại được tìm thấy nhau. Xin Chúa thương nhậm lời Ben, cho Ben được hưởng ngàn thu bình an bên Chúa. Nếu có thể, xin Ben lại ghé thăm anh trong những giấc mơ tiếp theo nhé, dù chỉ là một lời chào hay một nụ cười thân thương như ngày nào.

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Ben, my sweet boy, I miss you so much. Thank you for visiting me and Chú Chris last night. He told me he saw you flying a helicopter—so free, joyful, and strong up there. Down here, Mom and I are crying more and more each day. A piece of my heart feels completely dead without you, Ben. Please watch over us, pray for your mom, your brother Ryan, and me, and give us the strength to keep going. We love you forever
